g.text: Residue of chain B, numbered as in the structure file
Predicted aligned error (PAE) of a contact in Å, median of 2 draws: written from 5 Å, bold from 10 Å. Not pLDDT
Stroke weight and opacity follow the model's pLDDT: a contact is drawn at the lower of its two ends' values, a residue at its
An interface has no centre. The residues of chain B that touch chain A stand in a column, as boxes, ordered along the
interface and not by their sequence: neighbours in the column are neighbours in space; those of chain A around it. A line is
a pair of residues, at the shortest of its contacts of one kind.
All 17 residues of chain B at the interface are shown, with 27 contacts.
PAE (predicted aligned error) is the model's expected error, in ångström, in placing one residue of a contact relative to the
other: low is confident, about 32 means no idea. It is not pLDDT, which line weight, dashes and ? show.
The PAE comes from 2 samples of the model (2 draws). The PAE of a contact is the median of its 2 values, not the largest,
which would rise with the number of draws whatever the model knows. Draw by draw the contacts shown here range over
0.4–7.4 and 0.4–11.1 Å. Chains A, B and C are copies of one another, and the model names them in another order in 1 of
these 2 draws: the chains of every draw were matched to those of the structure shown here, by superposition, before its
5 of the 25 residue pairs in contact have a PAE of 5 Å or more, written on their lines.
